record.paper_title: Open problems in billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry
record.original_question: In the simplified locally conformal symplectic cotangent-bundle equations for a Tonelli Hamiltonian with eta pulled back from the base, what is the physical interpretation of the force term proportional to minus the Lagrangian times the eta one-form?

evidence.quote: It would be interesting to understand physically

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth manifold and let $T^*M$ denote its cotangent bundle, equipped with the canonical symplectic form $\omega_0 = d\lambda$, where $\lambda$ is the tautological one-form. Let $\pi : T^*M \to M$ be the projection, and let $\eta$ be a closed one-form on $M$, whose pullback to $T^*M$ we also denote by $\eta$. The pair $(T^*M, \omega_0)$ together with $\eta$ defines a locally conformal symplectic (LCS) structure via the Lichnerowicz differential $d_\eta \alpha := d\alpha + \eta \wedge \alpha$. For a smooth function $H : T^*M \to \mathbb{R}$, the LCS Hamiltonian vector field $X_H$ is defined by $\iota_{X_H} \omega_0 = -d_\eta H$.

Assume that $H$ is a Tonelli Hamiltonian, i.e. $H$ is $C^2$, fiberwise strictly convex, and superlinear in the fibers of $T^*M$. Let $L : TM \to \mathbb{R}$ be the Legendre-dual Tonelli Lagrangian of $H$. Writing the LCS Hamilton equations in local canonical coordinates $(q,p)$ on $T^*M$ with $\eta = \eta_i(q)\,dq^i$, one obtains a system of the form
$$\dot q = \frac{\partial H}{\partial p}, \qquad \dot p = -\frac{\partial H}{\partial q} - L(q,\dot q)\,\eta(q),$$
so that, relative to the standard Hamilton equations on $T^*M$, an additional force term equal to $-L(q,\dot q)\,\eta(q)$ appears.

Problem: Give a physical interpretation of the additional force term $-L(q,\dot q)\,\eta$ appearing in these simplified locally conformal symplectic cotangent-bundle equations for a Tonelli Hamiltonian with $\eta$ pulled back from the base. In particular, identify a mechanical or thermodynamic mechanism (e.g. a friction/dissipation law, a non-conservative external forcing, or a gauge/conformal rescaling effect) that naturally produces a force proportional to minus the instantaneous Lagrangian times the one-form $\eta$, and justify the identification.
artifact.status_search_result: The question asks for a physical interpretation that is explicitly flagged as an interesting open desideratum in the LCS Hamiltonian/Lagrangian literature. Recent works on locally conformal symplectic cotangent-bundle dynamics and locally conformal Euler–Lagrange equations describe the formal structure of such force terms but do not provide a definitive physical interpretation of the $-L\,\eta$ term. No published resolution was located.

status_evidence.title: Conformal symplectic geometry of cotangent bundles
status_evidence.snippet: Develops LCS Hamiltonian dynamics on cotangent bundles with a closed one-form eta pulled back from the base.
status_evidence.claim: Sets the framework of LCS dynamics on T*M but does not address physical interpretation of the -L*eta force term.

status_evidence.title: Discrete Dynamics on Locally Conformal Framework
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces locally conformally Euler-Lagrange dynamics and the modified equations of motion.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the equations but leaves physical interpretation of the additional force open.

status_evidence.title: Locally conformally symplectic reduction of the cotangent bundle
status_evidence.claim: No physical interpretation of the force term is given.
